construct: A lateral medullary infarct, usually involving vertebral or PICA territory, can damage the nucleus ambiguus, spinal trigeminal nucleus/tract, spinothalamic tract, descending sympathetic fibers, vestibular nuclei, and inferior cerebellar peduncle. Nucleus ambiguus injury causes dysphagia, hoarseness, and impaired gag/cough functions.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Crossed pain-temperature loss, ipsilateral Horner syndrome and ataxia, dysphagia, hoarseness, and preserved limb strength localize to the lateral medulla; dysphagia/hoarseness specifically indicate nucleus ambiguus injury.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Hypoglossal nucleus injury causes dysarthria and tongue deviation but not the pharyngeal/laryngeal motor deficit in this crossed-sensory lateral-medullary pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The symptom localization makes nucleus ambiguus uniquely responsible for the dysphagia and hoarseness.
